observations: Search is now one legible editorial field: one outer rule, a Search label and an unframed native input. The former nested-box reading is gone.
Card tags and participation state are visually quieter; metadata no longer competes with deck title and card art.
Header, filter panel, campaign strip and deck cards now share the same low-radius, thin-rule geometry.
The warm paper canvas and restrained red/yellow accents remain intact.

matchingSignals: thin dark rules with sparse red rule accents
remainingDifferences: The desktop environment taxonomy expands into a dense multi-row control wall, while the official source generally keeps taxonomy compact and gives more visual mass to content/media.
The masthead includes a visible ellipsis/ring capsule copied from platform chrome and a down-arrow switch cue although neither communicates a real product action.
The page still relies on host card imagery rather than the official site's stronger editorial asset compositions; acceptable for this minimal host experiment but not equivalent to source fidelity.

maskedStructuralRecognition.method: Visually ignore card art, logo/brand text and hue; assess mass, borders, spacing and reading order only.
maskedStructuralRecognition.evidence: The navy masthead, paper field, low-radius ruled islands, compact editorial labels and title-first cards remain coherent after explicit imagery/color cues are discounted. The result is recognizably closer to the official editorial system than Attempt 8, but the masthead pseudo-chrome is not supported by that structure.
